result.title: Reglos: A Self-Evolving Personal Memory Agent with Recursive Self-Improvement
result.summary: Personal agents draw on past conversations to tailor their responses to each user. Their memory systems store and update what each user says, and coding agents now also rewrite the harness that turns this memory into the model's context. Such patches risk overfitting, because one tested only on the failures it targets can fix those cases and help nowhere else. We present Reglos, a training-free personal memory agent that tests whether harness changes help beyond the failures they were written to fix. Its self-evolving memory adds to each user's append-only record with every conversation, as new preferences supersede old ones and facts can be forgotten. Its harness improves through recursive self-improvement, in which a coding agent proposes patches from failure traces and a critic from a second model family screens each one for benchmark gaming. After the harness is frozen, a fixed evaluator decides which further patches to accept. With the same backbone behind every system, Reglos outperforms state-of-the-art memory systems such as Mem0, MemOS and EverOS, reaching 61.3% and 84.0% on PersonaMem-v2 and LongMemEval-S with Qwen3.8-27B, and 57.5% and 87.2% with GPT-5.6 Luna.

AI.brief_summary: Reglos 是一个免训练的个人记忆智能体：用追加式用户记忆记录偏好与事实的更新，并让编码智能体根据失败轨迹改写上下文构建流程（harness），再由另一模型家族的批评者筛查是否在刷榜。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文面向个性化对话记忆与 agent 工程自改进，其状态是用户事实而非推理期 latent 状态，不涉及视觉证据筛选、动态计算或停止决策，自查机制也仅针对基准刷分，暂无可供核查的 LVR 借鉴线索。
